newsitem.title: USA: Tenneco unit buys Argentine manufacturer.
newsitem.headline: Tenneco unit buys Argentine manufacturer.

text.p: Tenneco Automotive, a unit of Tenneco Inc., has acquired about 94 percent of Fric-Rot S.A.I.C., an Argentine manufacturer of shocks and other parts to make cars run smoother, for $52 million.
One of the sellers, Arvin Industries Inc., based in Columbus, Ind., said it sold its 31.4 percent stake for about $17 million and expected a pre-tax gain of about $11 million.
A spokesman at parent Tenneco Corp. said the Deerfield, Ill.-based unit acquired the remaining 27 percent from Anlika of Uruguay, 26 percent from Cofap in Brazil and 10 percent from Tower Fund.

Fric-Rot, based in Rosario, Argentina, is the nation's largest supplier of ride control products for automakers, including Peugeot, Renault, Volkswagen, Ford, Chrysler and Fiat. It is also Argentina's largest maker of replacement shocks and struts.
Fric-Rot, with 350 employees and expected 1996 revenues of $45 million, will operated as part of Tenneco Automotive's Monroe Auto Equipment unit under the name of Monroe Fric-Rot.

With sales of $3 billion, Tenneco Automotive is the leading worldwide manufacturer of ride control and exhaust systems for both original equipment and replacement markets. In August, it bought 100 percent of Minuzzi, Argentina's second largest exhaust manufacturer.
Tenneco is a diversified manufacturing company based in Greenwich, Conn., with 1995 revenues of $8.9 billion.
Tenneco's stock was unchanged at $45.50 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
